findings.title: The stated cause of the 2R misses rests on Spearman correlations over near-identical shortlist members, and the redesign example it suggests cannot fix 2R
findings.detail: The spec (expected_outcome.A1) and note §3 attribute the 2R A1 misses to 'an L1/L2 disagreement near the optimum', citing within-shortlist Spearman correlations of L1 rank vs L(0.5 mm) of −0.95 to 0.25. In every 2R search shortlist, all 8 members' L(0.5 mm)/L(W*) − 1 lie within 0.0000–0.0012 of each other (5 of 8 shortlists within 0.0003). That is below the 0.25 % level-to-level q spread the note itself reports, so those correlations rank noise between near-duplicates. For example, draw 7 has ρ = −0.20 on a spread under 1e-5. The misses themselves are 0.2–3 points above the 2 % line. Re-ranking any existing 2R shortlist at L2 could change s by about 0.1 point at most. The data do support a different statement: the search's L1 basin sits 2–5 % above W* at L2 (L1 indicator 5/8 within 2 % vs L2 2/8; 2R search ≈ proxy-alone s). They do not support within-shortlist misranking. The note's Speculation ('a larger L2 shortlist, or an L2 re-ranking step on 2R, would address F4') and founder decision 1(a)'s example ('L2 re-ranking of a larger shortlist') therefore point the founder's redesign choice at a remedy the dev data show to be ineffective, at least for re-ranking alone. The headline numbers are unaffected.
findings.suggested_check: Replace the Spearman argument with the shortlist L spread vs the miss size, and qualify decision 1(a) so that within-shortlist re-ranking is not presented as a candidate fix for 2R.

findings.title: The spec promises 'fixed-shift stress rows' for the common-mode error that do not exist
findings.detail: config.joint_operating_characteristic.c_definition says the old σ_k construction 'is replaced by the fixed-shift stress rows below'. No such rows exist in the spec, in dev_rows.json (joint_oc has no shift key) or in the note. joint_oc's `shift` argument is never exercised. O008 scope_in asks the joint OC to include the common-mode error of the single L_sub(W*) solve. Under the revised estimand that error is only the solver tolerance (~2e-5), so the promised stress test is the only remaining sensitivity to a common-mode offset. My own bootstrap (B = 20000) with c_k = ±median b_k/2, ±median b_k and +max b_k gives P(PASS) ≤ 0.0004 in every case, because a shift that lifts A1 on 2R also removes Case 4 compact's resolved failures. The decision is therefore unaffected; this is a completeness defect.
findings.evidence: grep 'stress|shift' in E011.yaml finds only line 144. dev_rows.json joint_oc keys have no stress entry. Independent shift bootstrap: P(PASS) 0 / 0 / 0.00025 / 0.0004.
findings.suggested_check: Add the joint_oc(shift=±median b) rows to dev_rows.json and the spec, or delete the sentence.

findings.title: The upper-bound figure for P(A1 on 2R) is slightly understated
findings.detail: Note §5 says the one-sided 95 % upper bound on 2R's per-draw pass rate (2 of 8) is 0.59 and gives P(A1 on 2R) of about 0.09. The exact Clopper-Pearson upper bound is Beta⁻¹(0.95; 3, 6) = 0.5997, and P(Bin(8, 0.5997) ≥ 7) = 0.106. This is the decision-relevant (upper) bound on P(PASS), and it is about 0.11, not 0.09. The conclusion (do not register as is) stands.
findings.suggested_check: Recompute with the unrounded bound and state P(PASS) ≤ ~0.11 at 95 %.

findings.title: The spec records only an uninformative lower bound on P(PASS)
findings.detail: joint_operating_characteristic.values gives bonferroni_lower_bound_P_PASS 0.0. A recommendation not to register needs an upper confidence bound on π, which appears only in the note's prose (and is slightly misstated, see above). The plug-in bootstrap is degenerate at 0/8 and 8/8, as the note acknowledges.
findings.suggested_check: Add a one-sided upper bound on π (≈0.11 from 2R A1 alone) to config.joint_operating_characteristic.values.

findings.title: The selection-error bound is extrapolated from layouts that are not shortlist members
findings.detail: The 0.25 % (2R) and 0.48 % (Case 4) bound on how much the registered 0.25 mm selection could lower s uses q = L(0.25)/L(0.5) over 51 and 50 other layouts. No non-best shortlist member was solved at 0.25 mm. The direction is right (dev s is an upper bound on the registered s, so the OC is conservative for A1 and A3). For 2R draw 2, a paired win over compact needs s to drop by 0.27 points, against a 0.25 bound, so A3 on 2R is closer to flipping than the text suggests. The verdict is not affected, because 2R misses A1 regardless.

Recomputed s for all 96 rows and R_D from the raw em_lat0.25_<fp>.json solver files, independent of L2Table: max abs difference 0.0. Confirmed choose_proxy keeps the descent on both layouts (ratios 0.9376, 0.7176).

Hand-recomputed A1 (2R 2/8, Case 4 8/8), K1 (2R median 0.0297) and the A3 counts (2R compact 6 resolved / 6 paired; Case 4 compact 4 resolved / 8 paired; widen 8/8 on both) from the s, b and capped columns. Also checked ablation A1/K1 (c: 0, 0.093; e: 0, 0.059).

Independent joint-OC bootstrap (my own code, seed 12345, B = 20000): P(A1) 0.00025, P(A3) 0.234, P(PASS) 0, against the reported 0.0003, 0.226, 0. Exact binomials: 3.8e-4 for A1 at p = 0.25, 0.367 for paired 6/8, 0.637 for resolved 4/8. These match the per-layout figures within Monte Carlo error.

Checked Clopper-Pearson figures: 8/8 lower bound 0.6877 with tail 0.2317 ✓; 1/16 upper bound 0.264 ✓; Bonferroni A1 CI (0.022, 0.694) ✓; 2/8 upper bound 0.5997 with tail 0.106 (the note says 0.59 / 0.09).
Common-mode shift stress that the spec promised and omitted: c_k = ±median b/2, ±median b and +max b. P(PASS) ≤ 0.0004 in all cases.
Recomputed frozen_sha256 with canon_sha: it matches 5f540d0a…; setting band_bound.development_value back to null reproduces the old 61c7abc9…, so no other frozen value changed.

Computed the L(0.5 mm) spread inside every search shortlist. 2R spreads are 0.0000–0.0012, which undermines the within-shortlist Spearman / L1-L2 misranking inference and the re-ranking redesign example.
Spot-checked measured sizing from the solve files: 0.25 mm median wall 925 s (2R) and 3046 s (Case 4), max peak 6.43 and 16.53 GB, 743 em results. All match the note.
caveats: The headline result (on the dev draws: A1 0.25, A3 0, verdict INCONCLUSIVE; joint OC P(PASS) ≈ 0, so do not register as is) is reproduced and robust. The mechanism attributed to the 2R misses (within-shortlist L1/L2 misranking) is not supported by the data, and L2 re-ranking of the existing shortlist should not be treated as a candidate fix for 2R in founder decision 1(a).

The joint OC rests on 8 development draws per layout, resampled as i.i.d. given W* and independently across layouts. It is a planning figure, and the decision-relevant 95 % upper bound on P(PASS) is about 0.11 (from 2R's A1 alone), not 0.09.
The common-mode-error sensitivity that O008 scope_in asks for and the spec says is 'below' is absent. My independent stress shows it would not change the conclusion.

Dev search s uses 0.5 mm shortlist selection, whereas the registered rule selects at 0.25 mm. The joint OC is therefore conservative for A1 and A3. The bound on the difference (0.25 % / 0.48 %) is extrapolated from layouts outside the shortlists.
Cost and makespan options (A/B/C) were checked only for their measured inputs (walls, peaks), not for the scheduling simulation or pricing assumptions, which the note itself flags as unchecked.
